newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH REACH F.A. CUP FINAL FOR FIRST TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH REACH F.A. CUP FINAL FOR FIRST TIME.

text.p: Middlesbrough reached the F.A. Cup Final for the first time in their 121-year history after finally overcoming giantkillers Chesterfield 3-0 in a semifinal replay at Hillsborough on Tuesday.

Middlesbrough won with goals from Mikkel Beck, Fabrizio Ravanelli and Brazilian midfielder Emerson to end the stubborn resistance of the second division side who held them to a 3-3 draw at Old Trafford. They now face Chelsea in the final at Wembley on May 17.

Danish striker Beck put Middlesbrough ahead after 12 minutes when he scored with a shot that went in off the far post after a through-ball from the inspirational Juninho split the Chesterfield defence.

Juninho, who had an outstanding match, had what appeared to be a perfectly good goal controversially disallowed 13 minutes later when referee David Elleray blew for shirt-pulling by Beck on Jamie Hewitt just before the Brazilian appeared to have scored a perfectly good goal.
But Juninho was happier in the 57th minute when he whipped in a free-kick from the left which Ravanelli nodded home from close range.
The final goal came a minute from time when Ravenelli set up Emerson for a shot and the Brazilian lashed the ball home from 22 metres.
